title: Hosts (node_exporter)
description: The hosts outside the Kubernetes clusters -- file01 and the Proxmox hypervisors -- as node_exporter sees them. Provisioned by roles/node_exporter_scrape; edits made in the UI are overwritten on the next Ansible run. ZFS has its own dashboard.

panels.title: Hosts
panels.description: One row per host. Everything here is also a panel below; this table is for working out which host to look at.

panels.title: Load average, per core
panels.description: Divided by core count, so 1 means the host is exactly as loaded as it has CPUs, regardless of how many that is. The dashed line is where NodeLoadHigh fires.

panels.title: Memory in use
panels.description: Total minus available -- i.e. excluding page cache and reclaimable slab, which are not memory pressure. On file01 most of the rest is the ZFS ARC; see the ZFS dashboard.

panels.title: Filesystems
panels.description: ZFS datasets show up here too, as the filesystem collector sees them -- but on a copy-on-write filesystem the number that matters is pool capacity, not dataset free space. Use the ZFS dashboard for that.

panels.title: Disk utilisation
panels.description: Share of wall-clock time the device spent with I/O in flight. Sustained 100% means the disk, not the CPU, is the limit.

panels.title: Network errors and drops
panels.description: Flat zero is the expected shape. Anything else is a cable, an optic or a driver -- the fksw dashboard sees the other end of the same link.
